To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
EWS- FLI1-repressed transcriptional sub-signatures are enriched in FOXO1 binding sites and that EWS- FLI1 represses FOXO1 activity by direct binding and posttranslational modification.
EWS- FLI1 suppresses FOXO1 and that FOXO1 re-activation by MSA is a promising strategy for future EWS-FL1-specific therapy.
EWS- FLI1 suppresses FOXO1 expression by direct promoter binding as well as post-translational regulation, which results in a FOXO1-dependent growth regulatory sub-signature of repressed genes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification and functional characterization of a novel EWS-FL1-repressed gene regulatory sub-signature in Ewing sarcomas.
the identification of the EWS-FL1 transcriptional repressive signature and the characterization of FOXO1 as an important regulator of EWS- FLI1-repressed gene expression in Ewing sarcomas.
a previously unknown aspect of the EWS-FL1 oncoprotein, namely its repression of FOXO1 and its downstream target genes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the transcription factor FOXO1 is a novel target of the EWS-FL1 oncogene in Ewing sarcomas and that its suppression is required for EWS-FL11-mediated transformation.
FOXO1 is a major repressor of EWS-Flil1 in ES, and that its activation may be an effective therapeutic strategy for the treatment of ES.
FOXO1 is a novel EWS-FL1 target and that its reactivation by small molecule inhibitors may be a promising approach for a novel ES therapy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the EWS-FLIs of ES are able to suppress FOXO1 expression and activity by multiple mechanisms.
EWS- FLI1 is able to suppress FOXO1 activity by direct promoter binding as well as by phosphorylation of FOXO1, which leads to a nuclear export and an inactivation of FOXO1.
EWS-Flil represses the FOXO1 gene and that FOXO1 is an important regulator of a subset of EWS-Fil repressed genes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the aberrant transcriptional regulator EWS-FL1 can be targeted by small molecules that restore FOXO1 expression.
EWS- FLI1 represses a subset of FOXO1-regulated genes and that this repressive function can be exploited to treat Ewing sarcoma.
EWS- FLI1 is not only a potent oncogenic transcription factor but also a potent repressor of transcription.
